Algeria’s lower house has adopted a law allowing the death penalty for people convicted of deliberately setting fire to forests, woods or fields, following deadly wildfires across the country.  The amendment to the penal code was approved by the National People’s Assembly after President Abdelmadjid Tebboune called for tougher penalties.  No execution has been carried out in Algeria since 1993. #algeria #wildfire #news

The lush green forests of Seraïdi, overlooking the Mediterranean. And Constantine, a city built dramatically across cliffs and deep gorges, connected by bridges suspended high above the landscape.
